name: Sphinx, Crocosphinx
body:
Crocosphinx
CR 12

This squat-bodied beast resembles a pale-coated lion with a massive crocodilian head surmounted by a regal crown and jewels, with a pair of bulky, gray-feathered wings.

XP 19,200
CE Large magical beast
Init +3; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, true seeing; Perception +23

DEFENSE

AC 28, touch 8, flat-footed 28 (–1 Dex, +20 natural, –1 size)
hp 168 (16d10+80)
Fort +15, Ref +9, Will +11

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., fly 60 ft. (poor), swim 40 ft.
Melee bite +21 (3d8+6/19–20 plus grab), 2 claws +21 (2d8+6)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks death roll (3d8+9 plus trip)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 16th; concentration +18)

Constant—true seeing
3/day—dimension door (self only)

STATISTICS

Str 23, Dex 8, Con 20, Int 13, Wis 18, Cha 15
Base Atk +16; CMB +23 (+25 drag or sunder, +27 grapple); CMD 32 (34 vs. drag and sunder, 36 vs. trip)
Feats Cleave, Flyby Attack, Improved Critical (bite), Improved Drag, Improved Initiative, Improved Sunder, Iron Will, Power Attack
Skills Fly +1, Intimidate +18, Perception +22, Stealth +3, Swim +24
Languages Common, Sphinx
SQ absorbent wings, hold breath

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Death Roll (Ex)

When grappling a foe of its size or smaller, a crocosphinx can perform a death roll upon making a successful grapple check. As it clings to its foe, it tucks in its legs and rolls rapidly, twisting and wrenching its victim. The crocosphinx inflicts its bite damage and knocks the creature prone. If successful, the crocosphinx maintains its grapple.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm marshes or rivers
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Crocosphinxes are more chimeric in their appearance than most of their kin, having not only a bestial crocodilian head with massive jaws but also a long, thick, plated reptilian tail rather than the tufted leonine tail of other sphinxes. They are extremely aggressive predators, lairing alongside rivers and in oases that dot the desert wastes. Ordinary crocodiles instinctively recognize them and attend them with reverence, and the crocosphinx may even mate with the largest and strongest crocodiles in its domain. Their hunting habits resemble those of common crocodiles, often lurking just at the water’s surface with only their eyes and the tops of their heads exposed, with little to distinguish them from an ordinary crocodilian as they drift along. When they erupt from the water, however, their onset can be terrifying in the extreme, with sodden fur, thrashing tail, and whipping wings dazing their foes in a tumult of terror.
